newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World stresses need to promote biotech crops.
newsitem.headline: Oil World stresses need to promote biotech crops.

text.p: The use of biotechnology in food and farming needed to be communicated to sceptical consumers, the weekly independent newsletter Oil World said on Tuesday.

Information campaigns should focus on allaying fears they posed health and environmental risks and demonstrate the need to raise oilseed and grain yields in order to feed a growing world population from limited arable land reserves.
Crop engineering could be expected to provide solutions to these challenges through cost savings resulting from lower herbicide use and higher yields, due to lower chemicals input.
This may help cultivate presently marginal land.
Oil World said genetically altered soybeans, in the firing line especially in Germany, accounted for half the world output of oilseeds and soymeal for 60 percent of world meal supply.
The soy oil share in Germany's oil use was 23 percent, allowing subsitution, but in Brazil, it was 85 percent.
EU legislators should provide a satisfactory labelling option for genetically modified organisms, Oil World said.

While the bulk of U.S. soybeans could be expected to be modified in future -- and bioengineering of maize and rapeseed was in the pipeline -- European countries might wish to develop markets of costly soya products free from gene manipulation.
